standards.import_error_not_s1p: The selected file is not a .s1p Touchstone file.
standards.import_error_permittivity:
This file is a permittivity export (εr), not an S11 measurement.

It was saved as .s1p only so Touchstone viewers can plot it; it cannot be used as a calibration standard or as the sample.
standards.import_error_not_s11:
The file does not look like S11: |S11| reaches {peak:.3g}, while a reflection coefficient stays near or below 1.

It probably holds an already computed permittivity (as many .s1p files from the UTN 2021/2024 campaigns do).
standards.preset_save_no_data: No measurement to save. Measure or import first.
standards.preset_bundled_overwrite_msg: "{n}" is a preset shipped with the program and cannot be overwritten. Choose another name.
standards.precal_no_liquid_msg: Measure, import, or select a preset for the liquid before applying OPEN normalization.
standards.precal_description:
Place the probe in open air (OPEN) and measure. Normalization divides the liquid S₁₁ by the OPEN S₁₁, correcting cable and connector effects.

s₁₁_norm = s₁₁_liquid / s₁₁_OPEN
standards.temperature_reminder_preset: Preset recorded at {temp:.1f} °C: this liquid's known εr is evaluated at that temperature (session: {session:.1f} °C).
standards.show_indicative_tooltip: Theoretical S11 of the reference liquid (Debye εr through the probe's capacitive model). Hover its legend entry to see its source and parameters.
standards.indicative_tooltip:
Indicative reference (not calibrated)
εr: {liquid}, {model} (NPL tables)
Temperature: {temp:.1f} °C ({temp_source})
Probe: capacitive model Y = jω·C0·εr
C0 = {c0} pF ({c0_note}), Z0 = 50 Ω
standards.indicative_c0_generic: generic value, not fitted: pick the probe in Setup

open.name: Open (probe in air)
open.instruction: Hold the probe in open air — the face must not touch any surface or liquid. Cable natural, no forced bends. Sets the open-circuit reference (Γ ≈ +1) to correct cable and connector losses across the band.

short.name: Short
short.instruction: Contact BOTH inner and outer conductors on the probe face simultaneously — firm pressure, no air gap. Use a polished conductive disc or aluminium foil-wrapped foam. Short quality is CRITICAL: Γ ≈ −1, magnitude ≈ 1 across the full band.

reference.name: Reference liquid: {liquid}
reference.instruction: Immerse the probe in {liquid}. No air bubbles on the probe face. Check temperature. Then press Measure.

dut.name: Unknown liquid
dut.instruction: Immerse the probe in the unknown liquid, avoid air bubbles on the probe face, and keep the same temperature as the references. Then press Measure.

result.title: Permittivity Result
result.compute_failed: Could not compute permittivity. Please check that all calibration standards and the unknown liquid were measured on the same sweep.
result.all_gap: No physically valid permittivity could be selected on this sweep. Check the calibration standards and the reference liquids.
result.axes_caption: ε′ = real part (energy storage) · ε″ = imaginary part (dielectric losses). Faint grey curves are the other candidate roots.
result.equation_general: General form:  Gn·x^5 + x^2 + third_term = 0   (x = εr^(1/2),  εr = x^2)
result.criterion_text: Physical filter: Re(ε) > 0, Im(ε) ≤ 1×10⁻⁶  ·  Traversal: high → low frequency  ·  Seed: root with smallest |Im(ε)| at highest valid frequency  ·  Tracking: polynomial extrapolation (window 5, order ≤2) + nearest-neighbour  ·  Ill-conditioned points (|S₁₁ʳ¹ − S₁₁ʳ²| < 0.01) excluded as gaps  ·  With the simplified-method seed available, the root closest to that curve is chosen instead (the seed is also shown as the cross-check overlay)
result.simplified_note: ε_r comes from the closed-form cross-ratio formula (Higa 2016, eq. 18) using Short, Open (air, ε=1.0006) and one reference liquid — there are no candidate roots and nothing to override. The probe's radiation term is neglected, so accuracy degrades toward high frequency; for best accuracy use the full two-liquid method.
result.extend_msg:
Everything measured so far (Open, Short, {ref1} and the unknown) is kept. The wizard switches to the full two-liquid technique and only the second reference liquid ({ref2}) remains to be measured or imported — you can change it in the Configuration step.

The result will be recomputed with the degree-5 solver, seeded by the simplified curve shown here.
